people._note: The venue's about page names only a first name: 'Executive Chef & Owner · Wayne'. A travel guide adds that the restaurant is 'Run by a British chef and his Turkish wife'; no surname is published anywhere found.

_people_sources.note: 'Run by a British chef and his Turkish wife'

tripadvisor._note: Read from the Google knowledge panel's TripAdvisor snippet and Restaurant Guru's mirror. TripAdvisor itself returned 403 to every fetch attempt - see gaps. Wanderlog reported 4.5 / 1526 the same day.

operating_hours._recorded_from: The venue's own schema.org openingHoursSpecification, embedded in the JSON-LD on every page of vanillaantalya.com: Monday-Sunday, opens 11:00, closes 23:59. Chosen because it is the only per-weekday, machine-readable statement the VENUE ITSELF makes. It is NOT the only figure the venue publishes - see _conflicts.

_conflicts.where: venue's own config.php (VA_CONFIG.contact.hours) - this is what actually renders in the live 'Open now' badge and the footer once the page hydrates
the un-hydrated HTML of every page, the og:description meta tag, and the i18n 'footer.contact.hours' string in ALL 14 languages
contact page hero paragraph AS RENDERED in English in a real browser
Restaurant Guru JSON-LD openingHours, page says 'Updated 12 days ago'

operating_hours._note: SEVEN DISTINCT OPENING-HOUR STRINGS were found, four of them on the venue's OWN site, two of those differing by display language on the same page. The only figures that agree across independent parties are Google's and Restaurant Guru's 11:30-23:30. NO SOURCE ANYWHERE publishes different hours for different weekdays - every source states one range for all seven days.
operating_hours._seasonality: NOT PUBLISHED. Antalya venues commonly run later in summer, but NO source found - the venue's site, Google, Restaurant Guru, meyhankoli or any listing - states a summer/winter split, a seasonal close, or a seasonal terrace schedule for this venue. The hours above are what was published on 2026-09-05 and carry no seasonal qualifier. Do not read them as year-round.

seating.seats_basis: NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE. Cvent lists this venue as an event space and shows a dash for every capacity field - total meeting space, seating capacity, standing capacity, guest rooms. No listing, guide, review or the venue's own site states a seat, table or cover count. Left null rather than derived.

popular_times._status: MEASURED - published by Google, not derived here.
popular_times._units: Google's own relative busyness index, 0-100, scaled to THIS venue's own busiest hour (Saturday 20:00 = 100). These are NOT covers, NOT guests and NOT comparable between venues.
popular_times._day_index_basis: Google's own data-day attribute: 1=Monday .. 7=Sunday. Verified against the panel's aria-checked day, which was data-day=6 / 'Saturday' on Saturday 2026-09-05.

peak_windows.label: Saturday night peak
peak_windows.evidence: Google popular times, Saturday: 19:00=93, 20:00=100 (the venue's week maximum), 21:00=89. Google's own label at 20:00 is 'Usually as busy as it gets'.

peak_windows.label: Sunday late-afternoon peak
peak_windows.evidence: Google popular times, Sunday: 15:00=78, 16:00=93, 17:00=89, 18:00=85 - the week's second-highest block, and it peaks in the AFTERNOON, not at dinner.

quietest_day.evidence: Thursday's maximum across the whole week is 44 (at 20:00) - the lowest daily maximum of the seven. Friday is second-lowest at 46.

service_rhythm.weekend_shape_note: The measured curve contradicts the usual Friday/Saturday assumption: SATURDAY is by far the busiest day (peak 100) and SUNDAY is second (peak 93, in the afternoon), while FRIDAY is the second-QUIETEST day of the week (peak 46). Any simulated week must follow the measured curve, not the assumption.
service_rhythm.turn_time_note: NOT PUBLISHED. No source states a turn time, a seating length, a table-hold policy or a last-seating rule.
service_rhythm.covers_note: NOT ESTIMATED. Unlike the Meyhouse profile, no covers figure is derived here, because the input a derivation needs - a seat count - is not published for this venue at all (see seating.seats_basis). Multiplying an unknown seat count by an assumed turn count would produce a number with no floor under it. The only traffic evidence that exists is Google's relative busyness curve above, which carries no absolute scale.

reservation_grid.channel: The venue's own form on booking.php; confirmation is by WhatsApp or email. No third-party reservation platform (OpenTable / TheFork / Quandoo) lists this venue.
reservation_grid.published_defect: The <option> list is out of chronological order: 15:00, 16:00, 17:00 and 17:30 are appended AFTER 22:00 in the markup, so a guest scrolling the picker sees 12:00-14:00, then 18:00-22:00, then the afternoon slots last. Recorded verbatim in times_offered_verbatim.
reservation_grid.note: The first bookable slot is 12:00, an hour after the 11:00 opening the venue's JSON-LD claims and 30 minutes after the 11:30 Google publishes. The last is 22:00, 1h59m before the 23:59 close.

menu._currency_basis: Two independent confirmations on the venue's own pages: (1) menu.php's schema.org Menu markup gives every item an Offer with priceCurrency 'TRY'; (2) config.php ships currency.rates with TRY = 1 as the base and EUR/GBP/USD/RUB as derived multipliers. The page's own currency switcher defaults to ₺ (TRY). No price in this profile was converted.
menu._extraction_method: The menu is NOT an image. menu.php ships the whole card as a JavaScript array (const MENU = [...]) and mirrors it as schema.org MenuSection/MenuItem JSON-LD. The array was lifted byte-for-byte and parsed; names, prices and descriptions are the venue's own strings, including its typos. Nothing was OCR'd, so no price here is a visual guess.
_published_defects_carried_through: 'Beefeater Pink 4c', 'Don Julio Blanco 4c', 'Limoncello 4c' - the trailing 'l' of 'cl' is missing on three spirit rows.
'San Pelegrino 75c' - misspells Pellegrino AND drops the 'l' of 'cl'.

'Absolute Vanilla' for Absolut; 'Jaegermeister' for Jägermeister; 'Mon Réve' for Mon Rêve; 'Chardonay' inside the Signium description; 'Chivas Regal 12 Y.O' with no closing full stop while 'Macallan 15 Y.O.' has one.
'İced Mocha' carries a Turkish dotted capital İ while the other iced coffees use a Latin I.
'Vodka — by the bottle' is a SUB-HEADING shipped as an item row with no price.
'Buffalo Burrata' (1650) is printed twice - once under SALAD and once under PIZZA - with an identical description.
'Liqueur & Coffee' costs 750 under APERITIFS / LIQUEURS while 'Liqueur Coffee' costs 850 under HOT DRINKS.
'Mulled Wine' (600) is printed inside the RED WINES section.
'House Rose (70cl)' is printed as 70cl where the white and red house bottles are 75cl; the rosé carafe is named 'House Wine (500ml Carafe)' without 'Rose'.
menu._warning: Restaurant Guru hosts a Vanilla menu labelled 'Menu from owner a year ago' whose prices are systematically LOWER than the venue's current card: Guacamole 300 vs 550, Hummus 290 vs 460, Atom 300 vs 490, Dynamite Prawns 575 vs 850, Garlic Prawns 650 vs 890, Grilled Octopus 1150 vs 2750, Buffalo Burrata 875 vs 1650, Lamb Shank 1050 vs 2200, Fillet Of Beef 1300 vs 2250. It also lists items that are on the current card at a different price (Foie Gras De Canard 2200 vs 2550) and carries NO drinks at all. It was deliberately NOT used. Same for its 'Panko Crusted Goats Cheese Salad' spelling, which the current card writes 'Goat'.

pour_structure.spirits_single: 4 cl. Every whisky, vodka, gin, tequila, brandy, rum, aperitif and liqueur row on the card is a 4 cl pour.
pour_structure.spirits_double: NOT PUBLISHED. There is no double-measure price for any spirit except rakı. The card prices one pour size per spirit.
pour_structure.spirits_bottle: Listed but UNPRICED. 13 bottle rows (Vodka 50cl/70cl, Tequila 50cl/70cl, Whisky 70cl) appear on the card with an empty price field. See gaps.
pour_structure.raki: The only spirit sold in five published formats: 4 cl (single), 8 cl (double), 20 cl, 35 cl and 50 cl. Four brands x five sizes = 20 priced rows. The 20/35/50 cl rows are TABLE items, not per-guest items.
pour_structure.wine: Glass, 500 ml carafe and 75 cl bottle for each of the three house wines; glass + 75cl for the two Smyrna entry wines; every other wine is bottle only.
pour_structure.beer: Bottled/canned only, sized in the item name: 33cl, 44cl and 50cl.
pour_structure.sangria: One litre, priced 2250 - a jug for the table.

policies.service_charge_note: NOT PUBLISHED. No service charge, gratuity, KDV/VAT line, cover charge (kuver) or minimum spend appears anywhere on the venue's menu, booking form or site.
policies.allergen_note: No allergen or raw-item warning is printed on the menu. The menu does carry per-item dietary tags (vegan / vegetarian / gluten-free) and a diet filter, which is a different thing.
policies.reservation_policy: 'Nothing is charged online.' The form takes a date, a time from a fixed grid, a party size, a phone number with country code and an email; the venue replies to confirm, and the page says 'For the same evening, a quick call is best.'
policies.age_policy_note: NOT PUBLISHED. The site serves the full alcohol list with no age gate, unlike the Antalya runner-up The Barrels Pub, which gates its menu behind an 18+ confirmation.
policies.payment_options: 'Сredit cards accepted' per Restaurant Guru's feature list and 'Kredi Kartı' per meyhankoli. No card brands are published.
policies.parking: Restaurant Guru lists 'Parking' as a feature. No detail is published, and the venue is inside Kaleiçi's pedestrianised old town.

sources.note: no policy footnotes of any kind on the card

behaviour_notes.note: The night is drink-led and the drinks list is the deep half of the card: 46 alcoholic cocktails, 78 spirit rows, 37 wine rows, 6 beers and 48 non-alcoholic lines against 69 food rows. A simulated check here is beverage-heavy by construction, not by assumption.

Cocktails repeat within a single visit rather than opening it: a guest review says the amaretto sour was the one 'my fiancé couldn't stop ordering'. Model repeated rounds of the SAME cocktail on one check, not one cocktail per guest.

Three items on this card are TABLE items and must never be divided per cover: Sangria 1LT (2250), the 500 ml house-wine carafe (1500) and the rakı 20/35/50 cl rows (1550-3550). Rakı in particular is priced in five sizes per brand, so a rakı line can be anything from a 4 cl single to a 50 cl bottle at 3550.

The busiest hour of the week is SATURDAY 20:00 and the second-busiest block is SUNDAY AFTERNOON (16:00 = 93). Friday is the second-quietest day. A simulation that assumes a Friday/Saturday peak pair will be wrong about this venue in a way Google's own data contradicts.

Weekday traffic never collapses to zero between lunch and dinner - Monday runs 46-57 from 12:00 to 15:00 and stays 40-48 right through to 21:00. This is an all-day old-town room, not a two-service restaurant, which matches the venue's own 'Kitchen serves through the evening'.

Outdoor seating is the constrained resource, not the room: 'if you want a garden seat, it's best to make a reservation in advance', and the terrace is 'separated from the crowd by a glass screen'. Neither the terrace nor the room has a published seat count.
Bread arrives free and never rings: 'complimentary bread served with olive oil and balsamic vinegar' starts the meal. A zero-price cover item consumed on every check appears in no POS line.

Evening reservations step every 30 minutes from 17:30 to 22:00 while daytime steps hourly, so evening arrivals cluster on the half hour. Party sizes are bookable 1-8 online and anything larger is an '8+' free-text case the venue handles by WhatsApp.

The kitchen is a bistro kitchen with a Thai section, not a meyhane: 12 of 29 main courses are Thai (red curry, pad thai and fried rice, each in 3-4 proteins). Guests order it as the reason to come ('a killer pad thai'), so protein-variant lines on one check are the norm.

Rakı is on the card - 20 priced rows across Yeni Rakı, Tekirdağ, Efe Gold and Beylerbeyi Göbek - but there is NO SECTION NAMED MEZE to drink it with, unlike a meyhane; the nearest thing is a 12-row 'Appetisers' section that happens to include Hummus, Atom and Guacamole. meyhankoli nonetheless lists 'Meze Çeşitleri' and 'Meze Dolabı' (a meze cabinet) among this venue's features. The two sources disagree about whether meze is a named service here; the disagreement was not resolved.

Turkish listings classify this venue as 'Bar & Pub' with 'Egzotik Kokteyller' as a cuisine type, while its own site and every English listing classify it as fine dining. Both are true of the same room; a POS built only from the food menu would miss more than half the card.
Portion sizes run large - 'Be cautious about portion sizes as they tend to be large' - which pushes tables toward sharing rather than one main per cover.

Prices roughly doubled in about a year: nine dishes on the owner-supplied Restaurant Guru card from ~a year ago sit at 45-58% of today's price (Grilled Octopus 1150 -> 2750 is +139%). A profile of this venue goes stale fast; the read date matters.

Guests pay in several currencies' worth of expectation: the site ships a live currency switcher (TRY base, plus EUR/GBP/USD/RUB) and 14 UI languages. The prices are TRY; what a guest quotes back may not be.

gaps: Seat count, table count, terrace seat count and bar seat count: NOT PUBLISHED anywhere. Cvent, which exists to publish venue capacity, shows a dash for every capacity field.
Covers per service: not published and deliberately NOT estimated here - there is no seat count to derive one from.
Turn time / dwell / last seating: not published.
13 spirit BOTTLE rows (Vodka 50cl and 70cl, Tequila 50cl and 70cl, Whisky 70cl x9) are printed on the card with an EMPTY price field. All carry price: null.
4 wine rows are printed with an EMPTY price field: 'Antre' (white), 'Smyrna Shiraz-Petit Verdot (glass)', 'Mon Réve Tempranillo' and 'Mon Réve Montepulciano' (red). All carry price: null.
'Vodka — by the bottle' is a sub-heading shipped as a priceless item row; flagged is_section_heading_row rather than dropped.
Bottle size for 25 of the 31 bottle-listed wines: the rows print no volume. Only the house and Smyrna rows state 75cl / 70cl / 500ml. Not assumed.
Vintages, producers and grapes for most wines: the card prints a name and sometimes a region or grape in quotes, never a vintage. No vintage is recorded for any wine.
Opening hours are contradictory: seven distinct ranges across four venue-own locations and three third parties, two of the venue's own varying by display language on the same page.
Seasonal hours: NOT PUBLISHED. No source states a summer or winter variation for this venue, despite Antalya's seasonal norm.
Per-weekday hours: no source publishes a different range for any day - every source states one range for all seven days.
Service charge, VAT/KDV, cover (kuver), minimum spend, corkage and allergen policy: none published.

Live music: NOT ESTABLISHED. A 2019 meyhankoli review says 'Müzik kaliteli' (the music is good), which is evidence of music, not of live music or of a schedule. No source found states a live-music night, so none is recorded.
TripAdvisor's own page: 403 to every fetch, headless browser included. Its rating and count are recorded only as mirrored by Google and Restaurant Guru.
Trip.com, Yelp and Foursquare: blocked by a bot-verification wall or a login wall. Restaurant Guru's per-source review pages returned 503 on every attempt; only its summary page could be read.
Instagram posts: login wall. Only the profile header (followers, bio, one highlight title) could be read - no menu images, no event posts.
Absolute traffic: Google's popular-times values are a relative index scaled to this venue's own peak. There is no published number of guests, checks or covers for any hour.

Third-party descriptions of the concept are stale or wrong: Cvent says 'modern Italian cuisine, charcoal grilled steaks from grass fed cattle' and ArrivalGuides says the menu 'revolves around Italian cuisine'. Neither matches the current card. Not used.
